# Osprey: Browser Protection

> Osprey is a free, open-source browser extension that blocks phishing, malware,
> scams, and other dangerous websites before they load. It checks every site you
> visit against up to 21 threat intelligence sources through a privacy-preserving
> proxy that hides your IP address from those sources. For managed service
> providers (MSPs), the Osprey Management Console adds hosted multi-client policy,
> reporting, and alerting on top of the same free extension.

Osprey is operated by Osprey Project LLC, a California company. The ecosystem has
four parts:

- **Osprey (extension):** free, open-source, GPLv3 or later. No account, no ads,
  no paid tier, no upsell. Source: https://github.com/OspreyProject/Osprey
- **OspreyProxy (backend):** the open-source Java/Spring Boot service at
  api.osprey.ac that runs the threat lookups on the extension's behalf. MSPs can
  self-host it.
- **Osprey Management Console:** a commercial, hosted, multi-tenant console at
  https://console.osprey.ac for MSPs that manage Osprey across many client
  organizations. It is live but still in development and not yet accepting MSP
  customers. When it launches it will be sold only through MSP partners, never
  directly to businesses.
- **osprey.ac (website):** the public site, the free website safety checker, and
  the deployment tooling for administrators.

## Key facts about the extension

- **Cost:** Free. There is no premium version and no trial.
- **Browsers:** Chrome, Firefox, and Edge. Other Chromium browsers (Brave, Vivaldi,
  Chromium) work unofficially through the Chrome listing.
- **License:** GNU General Public License, version 3 or later (GPLv3 or later).
- **Operator:** Osprey Project LLC, a California limited liability company. The
  public proxy is hosted in New York, NY at api.osprey.ac.
- **Providers:** Up to 21 checks per site. 19 sources are routed through the
  Osprey proxy and enabled by default, grouped as official partners, DNS
  filtering services, and threat feeds. Additional providers such as MetaDefender
  can be enabled with your own API key, and those calls go directly from your
  device rather than through the proxy.
- **Permissions:** `tabs`, `webNavigation`, and `storage`, plus host access to
  `api.osprey.ac` (and to `api.metadefender.com` only if you add a MetaDefender
  key). Osprey requests no host access to the websites you visit and runs no
  content scripts, so it cannot read page content, cookies, or form data. This is
  enforced by the browser, not merely promised.
- **What is sent:** Only the address of the page you are opening. DNS-based
  providers receive just the hostname. API-based providers receive the full URL
  with query parameters stripped. Local threat lists are checked in memory on the
  proxy with no external call.
- **IP address:** Lookups are proxied, so providers see the proxy's IP address
  rather than yours, with thousands of users' checks mixed together. The proxy
  hashes IP addresses in memory for rate limiting and does not write raw IPs to
  disk.
- **Caching:** The proxy caches recent results, so most URLs are never sent to
  any provider.
- **Logging:** Safe results are never logged. When a provider returns a malicious
  or phishing verdict, a transient in-memory entry records the provider name, the
  verdict, and the checked hostname or stripped URL. It includes no IP address and
  no user identifier, is never written to disk, and is lost when the proxy
  restarts.
- **Localization:** The extension ships in more than 30 languages.
- **Architecture:** Plain Manifest V3 extension with no build system, a
  provider-based URL filtering design, a per-user allowlist, and a local detection
  log kept on the device.
- **Contact:** support@osprey.ac

## Website safety checker

Osprey runs a free website safety checker at https://osprey.ac/check/. You can
paste a single link and scan it on demand against the same providers the
extension uses, with the same proxy and query-stripping protections. The page
requires no account and uses Cloudflare Turnstile to prevent automated abuse.
Results are served from a short-lived scan store so repeat checks of the same URL
do not contact providers again.

## How it differs from built-in browser protection

Chrome, Edge, and Firefox each check sites against a single source. Osprey checks
up to 21 at once, so a site flagged by any one of them is blocked. Osprey is
designed to run alongside built-in protection and antivirus, not to replace them.

## Managed deployment for businesses and MSPs

The extension exposes managed policies that administrators set through Group
Policy (ADMX), Intune, macOS configuration profiles, Linux managed JSON, or
Firefox managed storage. Policy keys include:

- **Filtering:** `ManagedAllowlist`, `ManagedBlocklist`, `ManagedProviderSettings`,
  `CacheExpirationSeconds`, `MetaDefenderApiKey`.
- **Lockdown:** `LockUserAllowlist`, `DisableUserAllowlist`, `LockProviderSettings`,
  `HideProviderControls`, `DisableSettingsReset`, `DisableThirdPartyProviders`,
  `HideWarningProceedButton`, `HideWarningReportButton`, `DisableUninstallSurvey`.
- **Branding:** `BrandName`, `BrandLogoUrl`, `SupportUrl`, `SupportEmail`,
  `UserEmail`, `CustomWarningMessage`.
- **Backend and identity:** `ProxyBaseUrl` and `ProxyApiKey` to route lookups to a
  self-hosted proxy with a per-tenant key, plus `DeviceTag` and `SiteId` to
  identify the endpoint and client on reported events.
- **Remote management:** `ManagedConfigUrl` points at a hosted JSON document that
  is fetched on startup and every 60 minutes. Locally pushed policies always win
  over fetched values, the last good document survives outages, and the document
  cannot change its own source URL.
- **Reporting:** `ReportingEndpoint` and `ReportingAuthToken`. The extension posts
  detection and override events every 5 minutes and a health heartbeat every 15
  minutes, at-least-once with stable event ids. A missing heartbeat is how an
  administrator learns the extension was removed or disabled.

Self-hosted update channels let an MSP pin, stage, and roll back extension
versions on Chromium browsers through the force-install policy instead of the
public store.

Free tooling on osprey.ac supports this:

- [Deployment templates](https://osprey.ac/deployment/): ADMX/ADML, .reg files,
  Intune guide, macOS mobileconfig and plist, Linux managed JSON, Firefox policies.
- [Config generator](https://osprey.ac/config-generator/): pick policy values and
  download ready-to-push files for every platform. Runs entirely in the browser.
- [Reporting setup checker](https://osprey.ac/reporting-check/): a temporary
  receiver URL to verify that events and heartbeats arrive from a pilot endpoint.

## OspreyProxy

OspreyProxy is the Java and Spring Boot backend behind api.osprey.ac. The
extension sends each URL to `POST /{providerName}`, one request per enabled
provider, and the proxy forwards the lookup upstream with caching, request
coalescing, circuit breaking, and per-IP rate limits, then returns a verdict.
Providers are implemented as API lookups (such as alphaMountain, BforeAI,
ChainPatrol, iZOOlogic, PrecisionSec, URLAbuse), DNS resolvers (AdGuard,
Cloudflare, Control D, Quad9, Switch.ch), and in-memory local threat lists.
`POST /check` powers the website safety checker.

Operators can self-host the proxy. It expects a trusted reverse proxy such as
Nginx to terminate TLS and set `X-Real-IP`, exposes health and Prometheus metrics
only on an internal port, and offers an optional multi-tenant layer where every
extension request must carry a per-tenant `X-Osprey-Tenant-Key` with isolated
rate budgets and per-tenant usage metrics. It also includes the optional CRX update
server used for version pinning and rollback.

## Osprey Management Console

The Osprey Management Console (https://console.osprey.ac) is the commercial,
closed-source, hosted service for MSPs. It is still in development and is not
currently accepting MSPs; the features below describe what is built. The
extension stays free; MSPs will pay for the console, and billing is based on
active devices (those with a heartbeat in the
last 30 days, excluding archived devices). It is multi-tenant: each MSP is an
organization with many clients, and each client is a set of enrolled endpoints.

What the console does:

- **Enrollment:** generates per-client policy values and hosts the managed config
  document and reporting endpoint for each client, with ready-made enrollment
  scripts for NinjaOne, Datto RMM, ConnectWise Automate, and Kaseya VSA.
- **Policy management:** edit each client's allowlist, blocklist, provider
  settings, and branding from the console; enrolled devices pick up changes on
  their next refresh. Named baseline profiles can be propagated to many clients
  with drift detection when a client diverges.
- **Fleet visibility:** a cross-client overview with deployment coverage
  (enrolled versus expected seats), offline devices, outdated versions, pending
  requests, and recent events; a devices view with version and heartbeat state;
  and global search across clients, devices, and event hostnames.
- **Detection triage:** events carry a status (new, investigating, resolved,
  ignored), an assignee, and notes so technicians can work a queue.
- **Alerts:** per-client alerts for detections, bypasses, and missing heartbeats,
  delivered by email, webhook (with native Discord and Slack formatting), or PSA
  ticket. PSA integrations cover ConnectWise Manage, Autotask, HaloPSA, and a
  generic adapter.
- **Emergency fleet actions:** block or allow hosts across every client or a
  chosen subset in one action.
- **Unblock requests:** a public per-client intake page where end users request
  access to a blocked site; technicians approve or deny, and approval can
  allowlist the registrable domain or exact host in one click.
- **Reports:** scheduled branded PDF and email reports per client, plus an
  org-level digest, for quarterly business reviews.
- **White-labeling:** the MSP's brand name, logo, and accent color appear on
  report emails and PDFs, alert emails, webhook embeds, and the public request
  page.
- **Data controls (owner-only):** retention overrides, CSV exports, SIEM
  forwarding of every event to an HTTPS endpoint with retries and dead-letter
  counts, device auto-archiving after a configurable silent period, extension
  version pinning, API keys, and outbound webhook subscriptions.
- **Public REST API (v1):** bearer API keys (stored only as hashes, rate limited
  per key) can list clients, devices, and events, read fleet status, and run fleet
  block and allow actions. Outbound webhooks for detections, bypasses, missing
  heartbeats, unblock requests, and generated reports are signed with HMAC-SHA256
  in an `X-Osprey-Signature` header and delivered at-least-once.
- **Access control and security:** roles are Owner, Technician (staff), and
  Client Admin, with per-technician client scoping and strict tenant isolation.
  Sign-in supports passwords, passkeys (WebAuthn) with an optional org-wide
  passkey mandate, and OIDC single sign-on. Every state change is written to an
  audit log. PSA credentials and SSO secrets are encrypted at rest.
- **Operator messaging:** a message center lets the operator publish
  announcements and maintenance notices to every organization.

The console is built on Java 21 and Spring Boot with SQLite and an Astro front
end, and is reached through the Sign in link on osprey.ac.

## Pages

- [Home](https://osprey.ac/): What Osprey is, what it blocks, how it handles data, how it compares, and an FAQ.
- [Website Safety Checker](https://osprey.ac/check/): Scan a single URL on demand against Osprey's providers.
- [Download](https://osprey.ac/download/): Install links for Chrome, Firefox, and Edge, plus developer builds.
- [Deployment](https://osprey.ac/deployment/): Managed deployment templates for Group Policy, Intune, macOS, Linux, and Firefox.
- [Config Generator](https://osprey.ac/config-generator/): Build policy files for every platform in the browser.
- [Reporting Setup Checker](https://osprey.ac/reporting-check/): Verify a ReportingEndpoint configuration with a temporary receiver.
- [Management Console](https://console.osprey.ac): Sign in to the hosted MSP console (in development, not yet open to new MSPs).
- [Privacy Policy](https://osprey.ac/privacy/): Exactly what data is processed, sent, and retained.
- [Terms of Service](https://osprey.ac/terms/): Licensing, acceptable use, and disclaimers.
- [Source code](https://github.com/OspreyProject/Osprey): The full extension and proxy source.
